strong|You are a buy-side analyst checking management credibility for an Indian listed company. You get: (1) guidance items management gave on earlier earnings calls, each with an id and the call date; (2) the company's REPORTED quarterly and annual numbers (₹ Cr); (3) excerpts from the latest call. Use ONLY this data — no outside knowledge, no news. Tasks:
A) For each guidance id, give verdict: delivered | partial | missed | pending (period not over yet) | unverifiable (the numbers given can't test it). evidence: one sentence quoting the actual numbers (e.g. 'Q2 FY27 OPM 17% vs 18-19% guided'). cites: list of ids used, e.g. ["G3","Q:Sep 2026"].
B) credibility: one sentence overall read on promise vs delivery.
C) bull and bear: 3 points each, max 22 words each, each grounded in the data with cites (chunk ids like T1-4, or Q:<quarter>, or A:<year> for reported numbers).

verdicts.evidence: EBITDA was ₹47,517 Cr in Q1 FY27 and ₹56,616 Cr in Q2 FY27, still below the 2× target of ~₹95,000 Cr within three years.
No reported data confirms the arrival of the new ethane ship after the July 2026 call.
No IPO information is present in the reported numbers or call excerpts.
Capex figures for FY26 are not disclosed in the provided data.
Breakdown of FY26 capex into O2C, energy, Jio, retail is not available.
Revenue grew 6.1% YoY in Q2 FY26 and 10.4% YoY in Q3 FY26, below the 13‑14% target.
Segment EBITDA margins for RJIL and JPL are not provided.
RJIL operating revenue figures are not disclosed.

v.credibility: Management’s track record shows several unverified or unmet promises, indicating limited credibility.

bull.point: Revenue climbed from ₹239,986 Cr (Dec 2024) to ₹330,601 Cr (Sep 2026), a 38% increase.
EBITDA rose to ₹56,616 Cr in Q2 FY27, reflecting improving earnings.
Management highlighted strong polyester chain margins (+33%) and ethane price advantage, supporting future profitability.

bear.point: Q2‑Q3 FY26 revenue growth hit only 6‑10%, missing the 13‑14% target.
Key guidance on ethane ship delivery and Jio IPO lacks any verification, suggesting over‑optimism.
Stated EBITDA margins of 56.2%/51.8% are far above the reported ~15‑18% margins, indicating unrealistic goals.
